text_en: Bring 4 cups of water to a boil in a heavy pot. Add a pinch of salt.
Gradually add maize flour while stirring continuously with a wooden spoon to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat to low. Continue stirring and folding the ugali for 8–10 minutes until it pulls away from the sides of the pot and forms a firm, smooth ball.
Shape into a mound using a wet spoon. Serve hot on a plate alongside sukuma wiki, beans, or stew.
Wash rice and soak for 10 minutes. Drain and set aside. Brown beef cubes in oil for 5–7 minutes.
Add sliced onion and cook until golden. Add minced garlic and pilau masala, stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped tomatoes (if using) and cook until softened. Add drained rice and stir to coat with spices.
Pour in water and add salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 20–25 minutes until rice is tender and liquid absorbed.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot with kachumbari.
Mix flour and salt. Add water gradually and knead into a soft, smooth dough.
Divide dough into 6–8 balls. Cover and let rest for 30 minutes.
Roll each ball into a thin circle. Brush with oil, fold into a spiral, and roll out again gently.
Cook on a hot dry pan for 2–3 minutes per side, brushing with oil, until golden spots appear.
Peel cassava, remove the central woody pith, and cut into serving-sized pieces. Wash well.
Place in a pot, cover with water, and add salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 25–30 minutes until cassava is fork-tender.
Drain and serve warm, optionally with tea or a dipping sauce.
Peel arrowroot and cut into chunks. Wash under running water.
Place in a pot with water and salt. Bring to a boil.
Simmer for 20–25 minutes until tender when pierced with a fork.
Drain and serve hot as a snack or side dish.
Husk fresh maize cobs and remove silk.
Roast over hot charcoal or on a grill, turning frequently, for 10–15 minutes until kernels are charred in spots.
Sprinkle with salt and optionally squeeze lemon juice or dust with chilli powder. Serve hot.
Cut beef into cubes. Boil with salt and a little water until tender, about 30 minutes. Reserve broth.
Heat oil in a pan. Sauté onions until golden, then add garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a thick sauce.
Add boiled beef and stir to coat. Add reserved broth and simmer for 10–15 minutes until sauce thickens.
Adjust salt and serve hot with ugali or rice.
Brown goat meat in hot oil for 8–10 minutes in a heavy pot.
Add chopped onions and cook until golden. Stir in garlic, ginger, and spices.
Add grated tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Add water, cover tightly, and simmer on low heat for 1 to 1.5 hours until meat is very tender.
Adjust salt, garnish with fresh coriander, and serve.
Boil chicken pieces with salt and water until tender, about 25–30 minutes. Reserve broth.
In another pot, heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until softened and saucy.
Add boiled chicken and reserved broth. Simmer for 10–15 minutes until flavors meld.
Serve hot with ugali, rice, or chapati.
Slice liver into thin strips and rinse. Pat dry.
Heat oil and sauté onions until softened. Add garlic if using.
Add liver and cook on high heat for 3–4 minutes until browned.
Add chopped tomatoes and salt. Cook for 5–7 minutes until tomatoes break down and liver is cooked through.
Serve hot with ugali or rice.
Clean tripe thoroughly. Boil in salted water for 1 to 1.5 hours until very tender. Cut into strips.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic, ginger, and curry powder if using.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until softened.
Add boiled tripe and stir-fry for 5–10 minutes until well coated and heated through.
Adjust salt and serve hot.
Heat oil and sauté onions until soft. Add garlic if using.
Add minced beef and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Add chopped tomatoes and salt. Cook for 10 minutes until tomatoes break down.
Add water and simmer for 5–10 minutes until sauce thickens. Serve hot.
Boil beef ribs in salted water for 45–60 minutes until tender. Reserve broth.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic and ginger.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until thick.
Add boiled ribs and reserved broth. Simmer for 20–30 minutes until sauce coats the ribs.
Adjust salt and serve hot.
Clean and scale tilapia. Score the sides and rub with salt and lemon juice.
Heat oil in a deep pan until hot but not smoking.
Fry fish for 5–7 minutes per side until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with ugali and sukuma wiki.
Rinse omena well and drain. Optionally dry-fry in a pan for 2 minutes to remove excess moisture.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic if using.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until softened.
Add omena and stir. Cook for 5–7 minutes until well mixed and heated through. Adjust salt.
Serve hot with ugali.
Rinse dagaa and set aside.
Sauté onions in oil until soft. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add dagaa and water. Simmer for 5–7 minutes until flavors combine.
Adjust salt and serve hot with ugali or rice.
Cut Nile perch into fillets or chunks. Rub with salt and lemon juice.
Heat oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Fry fish for 4–5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with ugali or rice.
Soak beans overnight or boil for 5 minutes and let sit for 1 hour. Drain.
Boil beans in fresh water for 45–60 minutes until tender. Reserve liquid.
In another pot, sauté onions in oil until golden. Add garlic and tomatoes, cook until saucy.
Add cooked beans and some reserved liquid. Simmer for 10–15 minutes.
Add salt to taste and serve hot with ugali or rice.
Rinse green grams and boil in water for 30–40 minutes until soft.
In a separate pan, sauté onions until golden. Add garlic and tomatoes, cook until soft.
Add cooked green grams with some of their liquid. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Season with salt and serve hot with rice or ugali.
Boil pigeon peas in water for 40–50 minutes until tender.
Sauté onions in oil until soft. Add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add cooked pigeon peas and coconut milk. Simmer for 10–15 minutes.
Season with salt and serve with rice or chapati.
Roast groundnuts lightly, then grind into a paste or powder.
Sauté onions in oil until golden. Add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add groundnut paste and water. Stir well and simmer for 15–20 minutes until thickened.
Season with salt and serve hot with rice or ugali.
Soak kidney beans overnight. Drain and boil in fresh water for 45–60 minutes until tender.
Sauté onions in oil until golden. Add garlic and tomatoes, cook until saucy.
Add cooked beans and a little reserved liquid. Simmer for 10–15 minutes.
Add salt to taste and serve with ugali or rice.
Rinse lentils. Sauté onions in oil until soft. Add garlic and tomatoes, cook until saucy.
Add lentils and water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20–25 minutes until lentils are soft and stew is thick.
Season with salt and serve hot with rice or chapati.
Slice onions into thick rings and separate them.
Make a batter with flour, egg (if using), salt, and water until smooth.
Dip onion rings in batter and fry in hot oil until golden brown, about 2–3 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot as a snack.
Chop tomatoes and onion into small pieces. Finely chop fresh coriander.
Combine in a bowl. Squeeze lemon juice over and sprinkle with salt.
Toss gently and serve fresh alongside pilau, nyama choma, or any main dish.
Heat oil in a pot and sauté chopped onion until soft and golden.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a sauce, about 5 minutes.
Add shredded cabbage and grated carrot (if using). Stir to coat with the sauce and season with salt.
Add water, cover, and simmer on low heat for 10–15 minutes until cabbage is tender but not mushy. Serve hot.
Boil eggs for 8 minutes, cool, peel, and halve. Peel and cube potatoes, boil for 15 minutes until tender, then drain.
Heat oil and sauté chopped onions until softened. Add garlic and curry powder, stir for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until saucy. Add potatoes and spinach, stir for 5 minutes until spinach wilts.
Season with salt, top with halved eggs, and serve hot.
Wash kale, remove tough stalks, and slice finely. Set aside.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic if using and cook 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until softened and saucy.
Add kale and salt. Stir and cook for 5–7 minutes until tender but still bright green. Serve hot.
Remove thick stalks from collard greens, stack, roll tightly, and slice finely.
Heat oil in a wide pan. Add sliced garlic and ginger, cook until lightly browned.
Add the greens and stir until they brighten in color. Add chopped tomatoes, cover, and steam for 2–3 minutes.
Season with salt, stir, and serve immediately.
Peel and cut potatoes into chunks. Heat oil and sauté onions until golden.
Add garlic and chopped tomatoes. Cook until tomatoes break down into a sauce.
Add potatoes, salt, and water. Cover and simmer for 20–25 minutes until potatoes are tender and sauce thickens.
Serve hot with ugali or rice.
Peel and slice carrots into rounds. Heat oil and sauté onions until soft.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they soften into a sauce.
Add carrots, salt, and water. Cover and simmer for 10–12 minutes until carrots are tender.
Serve hot as a side with ugali or rice.
Finely chop green pepper, tomatoes, onion, and coriander.
Combine in a bowl and squeeze lemon juice over. Sprinkle with salt.
Toss gently and serve fresh alongside grilled fish, nyama choma, or pilau.
Preheat oven to 220°C. Prick sweet potatoes with a fork, rub with oil and salt, and place on a baking tray.
Roast for 45–50 minutes until fork-tender and lightly browned.
Split open and squeeze lime juice over. Sprinkle with chilli and a pinch of salt. Serve hot.
Heat oil and sauté onion and garlic until soft. Add diced pumpkin, cumin, and cinnamon, stir to coat.
Add water and bring to a boil. Simmer for 20–25 minutes until pumpkin is tender.
Blend until smooth. Stir in coconut milk and season with salt. Simmer 5 more minutes and serve hot.
Cut eggplant into cubes, salt lightly, and let sit for 10 minutes. Rinse and pat dry.
Heat oil and sauté onions, garlic, and ginger until fragrant. Add eggplant and curry powder, stir to coat.
Pour in coconut milk and simmer for 15–20 minutes until eggplant is soft and sauce thickens.
Season with salt, garnish with coriander, and serve with rice.
Wash okra and trim the tops. Cut into rounds. Heat oil and sauté onions until soft.
Add garlic and chopped tomatoes. Cook until tomatoes break down into a sauce, about 5 minutes.
Add okra, paprika, salt, and water. Stir gently and simmer for 10–12 minutes until okra is tender.
Serve hot with ugali or rice.
Heat oil and sauté onion until soft. Add chopped mushrooms and cook for 2–3 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes, stirring. Remove from heat and let cool for a few minutes.
Stir in yogurt and salt. Return to low heat and cook gently for 5 minutes—do not boil. Serve hot.
Wash amaranth leaves well and chop. Heat oil and sauté onion until golden.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until softened.
Add amaranth leaves and salt. Stir-fry for 5–7 minutes until wilted and tender. Serve hot.
Wash and chop cowpea leaves. Boil in water for 15–20 minutes until tender. Drain.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add cooked cowpea leaves and salt. Stir and simmer for 5–10 minutes. Serve hot.
Hard-boil eggs for 10 minutes. Cool, peel, and slice each egg lengthwise about three-quarters of the way through.
Finely dice tomato, red onion, and coriander. Mix with salt and a squeeze of lime.
Spoon the salsa into the split eggs and serve immediately.
Bring water to a boil. Add tea leaves (or tea bags), crushed cardamom, and grated ginger. Boil for 2 minutes.
Pour in milk and add sugar. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes.
Strain into cups and serve hot.
Peel bananas and break into chunks.
Blend yogurt, bananas, milk (if using), and sugar until smooth.
Pour into glasses and serve chilled.
Cut avocados in half, remove pit, and dice the flesh.
Dice tomatoes and finely chop red onion and coriander.
Gently toss everything with lime juice and salt. Serve immediately.
Mix flour, sugar, and water into a smooth batter.
Peel bananas and cut into halves or chunks. Dip into batter.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown on all sides, about 2–3 minutes. Drain and serve warm.
Peel green bananas and cut into chunks. Soak in water to prevent browning.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic and tomatoes, cook until saucy.
Add green bananas, salt, and water. Cover and simmer for 20–25 minutes until bananas are tender.
Serve hot with rice or as a side.
Rinse rice and drain. Heat oil and sauté onion (if using) until soft.
Add rice and stir for 1 minute. Pour in coconut milk, water, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid absorbed. Fluff and serve.
Dice mango and tomato into small cubes. Finely chop red onion and coriander.
Combine in a bowl. Add lime juice, chilli (if using), and salt.
Toss gently and serve fresh with grilled fish or chicken.
Cut passion fruits in half and scoop pulp into a blender.
Add water and sugar. Blend briefly.
Strain through a sieve to remove seeds. Chill and serve.
Soak tamarind pulp in 1 cup of hot water for 10 minutes. Mash and strain to extract juice.
Combine tamarind extract with remaining water, sugar, and grated ginger (if using). Stir until sugar dissolves.
Chill and serve over ice.
Peel papaya, remove seeds, and cut into cubes.
Squeeze lime juice over the papaya. Add chilli and chopped mint if using.
Toss gently and serve fresh.
Crush the garlic cloves and set aside. Heat oil in a heavy pot and brown the chicken pieces on all sides for 6–8 minutes.
Add chopped onions and cook until soft and golden, about 5 minutes. Stir in the crushed garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped tomatoes and salt. Cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until the tomatoes break down into a thick sauce.
Return the chicken to the pot, add water, cover and simmer on low heat for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce coats the meat.
Adjust salt and serve hot with ugali, rice or chapati.
Peel and grate or crush the fresh ginger. Bring water to a boil in a small pot.
Add the ginger and boil for 2 minutes to release its flavour.
Pour in the milk and add sugar. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 4–5 minutes.
Strain into cups and serve hot.
Blend fresh coriander, yogurt, garlic, ginger and green pepper (if using) into a smooth green paste.
Heat oil and brown the chicken pieces for 6–8 minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onions until golden. Return the chicken and stir in the coriander-yogurt paste.
Add salt and simmer on low heat for 15–20 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the sauce thickens. Serve hot.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Heat oil in a pot and sauté chopped onion and carrot (if using) until soft.
Stir in the turmeric and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the rice and stir to coat with the turmeric mixture. Pour in water and add salt.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 18–20 minutes until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed. Fluff and serve.
Heat oil in a heavy pot. Add sliced onions and fry on medium heat until deep golden brown, about 12–15 minutes.
Add minced garlic, grated ginger and pilau masala. Stir and fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add beef cubes and brown on all sides. Pour in 2 cups of water, cover and simmer until the beef is tender, about 30 minutes.
Add washed rice and the remaining water. Season with salt, stir once, cover tightly and cook on low heat for 20 minutes until the rice absorbs all the liquid.
Remove from heat and let steam for 5 minutes. Fluff gently and serve.
Grate the coconut and squeeze to extract about 1 cup of coconut milk.
Mix flour, ground cardamom, sugar and salt in a bowl. Add the coconut milk and egg (if using) and knead into a soft dough.
Cover the dough and let it rest for 20 minutes. Divide into small balls and roll each into a thin circle, then cut into triangles.
Heat oil in a deep pan and fry the triangles in batches for 2–3 minutes per side until golden brown. Drain and serve warm.
Mix flour, cinnamon and salt in a large bowl. Add water gradually and knead into a soft, smooth dough.
Divide the dough into 6–8 balls. Cover and let rest for 30 minutes.
Roll each ball into a thin circle. Brush with oil, fold into a spiral and roll out again gently.
Cook on a hot dry pan for 2–3 minutes per side, brushing with oil, until golden spots appear. Serve warm.
Melt the ghee in a heavy pan over medium heat. Add the flour and roast, stirring constantly, until golden brown and fragrant, about 8–10 minutes.
In a separate pot, combine sugar, water and cardamom. Bring to a boil to make a syrup.
Carefully pour the hot syrup into the roasted flour mixture, stirring vigorously to prevent lumps.
Cook on low heat, stirring, for 8–10 minutes until the mixture thickens and pulls away from the sides of the pan. Serve warm or at room temperature.
Rub the butter into the flour and salt until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs. Stir in the sugar.
Add the milk and egg (if using) and mix into a soft dough. Knead gently for 3–4 minutes.
Cover and let rest for 15 minutes. Roll out and cut into triangles or squares.
Fry in hot oil for 2–3 minutes per side until golden brown. Drain and serve warm.
Bring the fresh milk to a boil, then remove from heat and let it cool to lukewarm.
Stir in the sour milk as a starter culture.
Pour into a clean calabash or jar, cover and leave in a warm place for 1–2 days to ferment until thick and sour.
Stir well and serve chilled or at room temperature.
Peel the green plantains and cut into chunks. Soak in water to prevent browning.
Heat oil and brown the beef cubes for 6–8 minutes. Add chopped onions and garlic and cook until soft.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a sauce.
Add the plantains, salt and water. Cover and simmer for 25–30 minutes until the plantains are tender and the stew has thickened.
Serve hot with rice or as a standalone meal.
Peel the ripe plantains and cut into thick slices. Brown the beef in hot oil for 6–8 minutes.
Add chopped onion and garlic and cook until softened. Stir in chopped tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add the plantains, salt and water. Cover and simmer for 20–25 minutes until the plantains are soft and the beef is tender.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot with rice or ugali.
Rinse the rice. Heat oil and sauté chopped onion (if using) until soft.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute. Pour in water and add salt.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 18–20 minutes until the rice is tender.
Squeeze the lemon juice over the cooked rice and grate in some zest. Fluff gently and serve.
Wash and thinly slice the limes. Mix with salt and turmeric in a bowl.
Pack the lime mixture tightly into a clean glass jar.
Heat oil in a small pan and add the chilli flakes. Pour the hot oil over the limes.
Seal the jar and leave in a warm place for 2–3 days to mature before using.
Spatchcock the chicken by cutting along the backbone and flattening it. Pat dry.
Mix lemon juice, crushed garlic, paprika, oil and salt into a marinade. Rub all over the chicken and let sit for 20 minutes.
Grill over medium charcoal or on a barbecue for 30–40 minutes, turning occasionally, until the skin is charred and the chicken is cooked through.
Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into pieces and serve.
Cut the chicken breast into chunks and season with salt. Heat oil and brown the chicken for 4–5 minutes, then remove.
Sauté onion, garlic and ginger until fragrant. Stir in curry powder and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a simmer. Return the chicken to the pan and cook for 15 minutes until tender and the sauce thickens.
Stir in chopped coriander and serve hot with rice or chapati.
Marinate the chicken thighs with yogurt, garlic, ginger, pilau masala and salt for 30 minutes.
Par-boil the rice in salted water until half-cooked, then drain.
Fry the onions until golden. Add the marinated chicken and cook until browned and cooked through.
Layer the chicken and rice in a heavy pot, cover tightly and steam on low heat for 20 minutes.
Fluff gently and serve hot.
Heat oil in a pot and brown the chicken drumsticks on all sides for 6–8 minutes.
Add chopped onions and garlic and cook until soft and golden.
Add chopped tomatoes and salt. Cook until the tomatoes break down into a sauce.
Add water, cover and simmer on low heat for 30–35 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Serve hot with ugali or rice.
Slice the liver into thin strips and rinse. Pat dry.
Heat oil and sauté the onion until softened. Add garlic if using and cook for 1 minute.
Add the liver and cook on high heat for 3–4 minutes until browned.
Add chopped tomatoes and salt. Cook for 5–7 minutes until the tomatoes break down and the liver is cooked through. Serve hot.
Clean the tripe thoroughly and boil in salted water for 1 to 1.5 hours until very tender. Cut into strips.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic and curry powder (if using) and cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until softened into a sauce.
Add the boiled tripe and stir to coat. Simmer for 10–15 minutes, adding a little water if needed. Adjust salt and serve hot.
Boil the beef ribs in salted water for 45–50 minutes until tender. Reserve the broth.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a thick sauce.
Add the boiled ribs and a splash of reserved broth. Stir-fry for 10–15 minutes until the ribs are coated and the sauce is thick. Serve hot.
Soak the smoked fish in warm water for 10 minutes to remove excess salt. Drain and cut into pieces.
Heat oil and sauté onions until soft. Add garlic if using and cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they form a sauce.
Add the fish and water. Simmer for 10–15 minutes until the fish is heated through and the sauce is flavorful. Serve hot.
Soak the dried fish in warm water for 10 minutes, then clean and remove any bones.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until softened.
Add the fish and water. Simmer for 10–15 minutes until the fish is tender and the stew has thickened.
Season with salt and serve hot with ugali.
Rinse the black-eyed peas and boil in water for 30–40 minutes until tender. Drain, reserving some liquid.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic if using and cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a sauce.
Add the cooked peas and a little reserved liquid. Simmer for 10 minutes, season with salt and serve.
Rinse the yellow lentils. Heat oil and sauté onion and garlic until soft.
Add chopped tomatoes and curry powder (if using) and cook for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add the lentils, coconut milk, water and salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20–25 minutes until the lentils are soft and the stew is creamy.
Serve hot with rice or chapati.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Add chopped onions and fry until golden, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger and curry powder. Stir and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a thick sauce, about 8 minutes.
Add cooked chickpeas and 1 cup water. Stir well, season with salt and simmer for 15 minutes until sauce thickens. Serve hot.
Trim and cut the green beans into bite-sized pieces. Heat oil and sauté onions until soft.
Add garlic, curry powder and chopped tomatoes. Cook until the tomatoes soften into a sauce.
Add the green beans and coconut milk. Stir, season with salt and simmer for 10–12 minutes until the beans are tender but still bright.
Serve hot as a side with rice or chapati.
Slice the cucumber into thin half-moons. Dice the tomatoes and finely chop the red onion.
Combine cucumber, tomato, onion and coriander in a bowl.
Squeeze lime juice over, sprinkle with salt and toss gently. Serve fresh.
Finely dice the red onion and tomatoes. Chop the coriander and chilli.
Mix everything in a bowl with lime juice and salt.
Let sit for 5 minutes to soften the onion, then serve.
Finely chop the spring onions. Whisk the eggs with salt and black pepper.
Heat oil in a frying pan. Add the spring onions and cook for 1 minute until softened.
Pour in the eggs and cook on low heat until set, then fold and serve.
Bring water and salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Gradually add the sorghum flour while stirring continuously with a wooden spoon to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat and keep stirring and folding for 8–10 minutes until the ugali pulls away from the sides and forms a firm ball.
Shape into a mound and serve hot with a stew or greens.
Mix the millet flour with 1 cup of water to make a smooth paste.
Bring the remaining 3 cups of water to a boil. Stir in the millet paste and salt.
Cook on low heat for 10–12 minutes, stirring often, until the porridge thickens. Sweeten with sugar if desired and serve warm.
Bring water and salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Gradually add the ugali meal while stirring continuously with a wooden spoon to avoid lumps.
Reduce heat and keep stirring and folding for 8–10 minutes until the ugali is firm and pulls away from the pot.
Turn out and shape into a mound. Serve hot with sukuma wiki, beans or meat.
Mix millet flour with water to form a smooth paste.
Bring the fresh milk to a gentle boil. Stir in the millet paste and salt.
Cook on low heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy. Sweeten with sugar if desired and serve warm.
Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool, peel and slice each egg lengthwise about three-quarters of the way through.
Finely dice the tomato and red onion. Chop the coriander and chilli.
Mix the salsa with lime juice and salt. Spoon generously into the split eggs and serve immediately.
Wash and finely slice the kale. Heat coconut oil in a pan and sauté onions until soft.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they soften.
Add the kale and salt. Stir-fry for 5–7 minutes until tender but still bright green. Serve hot.
Heat groundnut oil in a pan and sauté onions until golden.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft and saucy.
Add the spinach and salt. Stir until wilted, about 5 minutes. Scatter with crushed groundnuts and serve.
Shred the cabbage finely. Heat oil and sauté onions until golden.
Stir in the curry powder and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add the cabbage and salt. Stir-fry for 8–10 minutes until tender. Serve hot.
Boil the beef with salt and water until tender, about 30–35 minutes. Reserve the broth.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic and chopped tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Stir in the mchuzi mix, then add the beef and reserved broth. Simmer for 15–20 minutes until the stew thickens.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot with ugali or rice.
Cut potatoes into chips and fry in hot oil until golden and crisp. Drain and set aside.
In a separate pan, sauté onions and garlic until soft. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down.
Stir in the garam masala and salt, then add the fried chips and toss until well coated. Serve hot.
Finely chop the chilli, tomatoes, red onion and coriander.
Combine everything in a bowl with lime juice and salt.
Toss and serve fresh with grilled meat or rice.
Brown the chicken pieces in hot oil for 6–8 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Sauté onions and garlic until soft. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Return the chicken to the pot, season with salt and simmer for 15–20 minutes until cooked through.
Stir in the chopped mint just before serving.
Bruise the lemongrass stalks with the back of a knife and place in a pot with water. Bring to a boil.
Add tea leaves and simmer for 3 minutes, then pour in the milk and sugar.
Simmer for another 3–4 minutes, strain and serve hot.
Mix the flour and salt. Add the milk and knead into a soft dough. Let rest for 15 minutes.
Roll out and cut into triangles. Fry in hot oil until golden brown.
While still warm, toss the mandazi in sugar until coated. Serve immediately.
Boil the beef until tender, about 30 minutes. Reserve the broth.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add the beef, diced green pepper and a little broth. Simmer for 10–15 minutes until the pepper is tender and the sauce coats the meat.
Season with salt and serve hot.
Season the tilapia fillets with salt. Heat oil and lightly fry the fillets for 2 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté onions, garlic and ginger until fragrant. Add chopped tomatoes and curry powder and cook until saucy.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer. Return the fish to the pan and cook for 10–12 minutes until the fish is cooked through and the sauce thickens.
Serve hot with rice or ugali.
Rinse the dagaa and drain. Heat oil and fry the dagaa for 3–4 minutes until slightly crisp. Remove and set aside.
In the same oil, sauté onions until golden. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down.
Return the dagaa to the pan, add water and salt. Simmer for 8–10 minutes. Squeeze lemon juice over and serve hot.
Season the Nile perch with salt. Heat oil and fry the fish for 3–4 minutes per side until golden. Remove and set aside.
Sauté onions and garlic until soft. Add chopped tomatoes and green pepper and cook until saucy.
Add water and bring to a simmer. Return the fish to the pan and cook for 10 minutes until heated through and the sauce thickens.
Serve hot with ugali or rice.
Soak the smoked fish in warm water for 10 minutes to remove excess salt. Drain and flake into pieces.
Heat oil and sauté onions until soft. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they form a sauce.
Pour in the coconut milk and water. Add the fish and simmer for 10–15 minutes until the stew thickens. Season with salt and serve.
Mix the millet flour with 1 cup of water to form a smooth paste.
Bring the remaining water to a boil. Stir in the millet paste and cook for 8–10 minutes until thickened.
Remove from heat and stir in the sour milk (and salt if using). Serve warm.
Heat oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef cubes in batches over high heat. Remove and set aside.
Add the sliced onions to the same pot and cook on medium-low heat for 10–12 minutes until soft, golden and sweet.
Stir in the garlic and chopped tomatoes (if using) and cook for 5 minutes until the tomatoes break down.
Return the beef to the pot, add salt and water, cover and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until the beef is tender and the gravy is thick.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot with ugali or rice.
